title: Strong El Niño to Bring Wet South and Mild North This Winter
summaryZh: NOAA冬季展望：強聖嬰現象將使美南多雨、北部偏暖。
summaryHi: NOAA: तेज़ एल नीनो से इस सर्दी अमेरिका के दक्षिण में ज़्यादा बारिश और उत्तर में गर्मी रहेगी।
summaryEs: La NOAA prevé que un fuerte El Niño traiga un invierno lluvioso al sur y templado al norte de EE. UU.
summaryJa: NOAA冬季予報：強いエルニーニョで米南部は雨が多く、北部は暖冬に。
summaryKo: NOAA 겨울 전망: 강한 엘니뇨로 미국 남부는 습하고 북부는 따뜻할 듯.
summaryEn: NOAA says a very strong El Niño will likely make the US South wetter and the North warmer this winter.
paragraphs: A very strong El Niño is expected to bring a wetter-than-usual winter to the southern United States and milder conditions across much of the north, according to the official outlook published on Thursday by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

El Niño, the warm phase of a natural cycle in Pacific Ocean temperatures, tends to push the jet stream south and east. Ken Graham, director of the National Weather Service, said this raises the odds of stormier weather across the South between December and February.

Above-average temperatures are favoured in the Pacific Northwest, the Midwest, much of the East and Alaska, while near-normal conditions are most likely in parts of the Southeast. Florida has the highest chance of above-normal rain, and parts of California and Arizona could also see a very wet season.

The extra moisture should ease drought in the Southwest, the Southern Plains and the Southeast. But Graham warned that too much rain falling on dry soil can trigger destructive flash floods and mudslides.
Forecasters stressed that the outlook expresses probabilities rather than certainties, and that it does not predict snowfall, which cannot be forecast reliably more than about a week ahead.
The US weather agency, NOAA, said on Thursday what this winter may be like. Winter here means December, January and February.
There is a very strong El Niño this year. El Niño happens when the sea in the Pacific Ocean is warmer than usual. It changes the weather in many countries.
NOAA says the north of the US will probably be warmer than normal this winter. This includes Alaska and states near Canada.

The south will probably get more rain than normal. Florida may be very wet. Parts of California and Arizona may get a lot of rain too. This is good news for dry places, because the rain can help them.
But there is also danger. Too much rain on dry land can cause floods. NOAA asks people to get ready for winter now. It cannot say how much snow will come.
The US weather agency NOAA released its winter forecast on Thursday, saying a very strong El Niño will probably shape the weather from December to February.
El Niño is a natural pattern that happens when the surface of the Pacific Ocean becomes warmer than usual. NOAA says it is very confident that a strong El Niño will be in place this winter.

Because of this, the northern part of the country, including the Pacific Northwest, the Midwest, much of the East and Alaska, is likely to be warmer than average. The South is likely to be wetter than normal, with Florida having the highest chance of extra rain.

The rain could help areas that are in drought, such as the Southwest and the Southern Plains. However, Ken Graham, the head of the National Weather Service, warned that heavy rain on dry ground can cause flash floods and mudslides.
NOAA said its forecast is about chances, not certain results, and it does not predict snow because snow is too hard to forecast more than a week ahead. The next update will come on November 19.

A very strong El Niño is expected to bring a wetter-than-usual winter to the southern United States and milder conditions across much of the north, according to the official outlook published on Thursday by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

El Niño, the warm phase of a natural cycle in Pacific Ocean temperatures, tends to push the jet stream south and east. Ken Graham, director of the National Weather Service, said this raises the odds of stormier weather across the South between December and February.

Above-average temperatures are favoured in the Pacific Northwest, the Midwest, much of the East and Alaska, while near-normal conditions are most likely in parts of the Southeast. Florida has the highest chance of above-normal rain, and parts of California and Arizona could also see a very wet season.

The extra moisture should ease drought in the Southwest, the Southern Plains and the Southeast. But Graham warned that too much rain falling on dry soil can trigger destructive flash floods and mudslides.
Forecasters stressed that the outlook expresses probabilities rather than certainties, and that it does not predict snowfall, which cannot be forecast reliably more than about a week ahead.

Americans should brace for a winter shaped by one of the most powerful El Niño events in recent memory, with the South likely to turn markedly wetter and much of the North set to escape the worst of the cold, according to NOAA's seasonal outlook released on Thursday.

The agency said it was highly confident that a very strong El Niño, the warm phase of the Pacific's natural temperature cycle, would persist through December, January and February. Such events typically displace the jet stream southward and eastward, steering storms across the southern tier of the country.

Warmth is favoured from the Pacific Northwest through the Midwest and much of the East, as well as in Alaska. Florida faces the strongest odds of a soggy season, with California and Arizona also in line for heavy precipitation.

While the rain should bring welcome relief to drought-stricken parts of the Southwest and the Southern Plains, National Weather Service director Ken Graham cautioned that downpours on parched ground can unleash flash floods and mudslides.

Scientists at the Climate Prediction Center emphasised that the forecast deals in probabilities and that local impacts will not always match the expected pattern. Snowfall, they noted, remains impossible to predict reliably this far ahead.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has forecast that an exceptionally strong El Niño will dominate weather patterns across the United States this winter, with significant implications for agriculture, water supplies and emergency planning.

El Niño refers to the periodic warming of surface waters in the tropical Pacific, which alters atmospheric circulation worldwide. According to the agency, the phenomenon is likely to shift the jet stream southward and eastward, thereby increasing the probability of frequent storms throughout the southern states between December and February.

Consequently, above-average temperatures are anticipated across the northern tier, including the Pacific Northwest, the Midwest and Alaska, whereas Florida, California and Arizona face a heightened likelihood of substantial precipitation.

Although this moisture is expected to alleviate prolonged drought in the Southwest and the Southern Plains, officials have emphasised that it carries considerable risk. Ken Graham, director of the National Weather Service, warned that intense rainfall on arid soil can precipitate destructive flash floods and mudslides, and he urged communities to prepare in advance.

Meteorologists stressed that the outlook is probabilistic rather than definitive, and that regional outcomes may diverge from the overall pattern. Snowfall totals were deliberately excluded, since they cannot be predicted with confidence beyond roughly one week.

noteJa.meaning: （悪い事態を）急に引き起こす。

noteJa.exampleTr: 金利の急上昇は住宅危機を引き起こしかねない。

noteKo.usage: 매우 격식 있는 타동사; crisis / collapse와 함께. 명사 precipitation은 '강수'도 뜻함.

noteEn.meaning: to make something bad happen suddenly or sooner.

precipitation.en: rain, snow or hail that falls

predict.en: to say what will happen in the future
predict.ex: No one can predict the future.

predicted.en: said what would happen in the future

prediction.en: a statement about what will happen

probabilistic.en: based on how likely things are

note.meaning: 機率性的、以機率表示的。
note.usage: 形容詞，學術用語；probabilistic forecast / model / approach；名詞 probability。

example.en: Weather services now give probabilistic forecasts for rain.
example.zh: 氣象單位現在以機率形式發布降雨預報。

noteHi.exampleTr: मौसम सेवाएँ अब बारिश के लिए संभाव्य पूर्वानुमान देती हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los servicios meteorológicos dan ahora pronósticos probabilísticos de lluvia.

noteJa.meaning: 確率的な、確率で表された。
noteJa.usage: 学術的な形容詞。probabilistic forecast / model。
noteJa.exampleTr: 気象機関は現在、雨の確率予報を出している。

noteKo.exampleTr: 기상 기관은 이제 비에 대해 확률 예보를 낸다.

noteEn.meaning: based on how likely different outcomes are, not on certainty.

probability.ex: The probability of snow is low.

note.usage: 形容詞，多修飾負面或需忍受的事：prolonged drought / illness / exposure / period。

example.en: Prolonged exposure to the sun can damage your skin.
example.zh: 長時間曝曬可能傷害皮膚。

noteHi.usage: अक्सर नकारात्मक चीज़ों के साथ: prolonged drought / illness।
noteHi.exampleTr: लंबे समय तक धूप में रहना त्वचा को नुकसान पहुँचा सकता है।

noteEs.usage: Suele acompañar cosas negativas: prolonged drought / illness.

noteJa.usage: 否定的な事柄を修飾することが多い（prolonged drought / illness）。
noteJa.exampleTr: 長時間日光に当たると肌を傷めることがある。

noteKo.usage: 주로 부정적인 것과 함께(prolonged drought / illness).
noteKo.exampleTr: 장시간 햇볕에 노출되면 피부가 손상될 수 있다.
